questions.ask: Is the inside shoulder wider on carriageways of 3+ lanes, and by how much?
questions.notes: Answered by DERIVATION only (no code states a 3+-lane rule): FHWA's 4 ft carries no lane-count condition. A state manual's own lane-count rule would supersede it — Quire's extraction may find one. ⸻ Caltrans (CA only, Quire 2026-09-23): YES by lane count — left shoulder 5 ft at 4 lanes total, 10 ft at 6+ lanes total (Table 302.1, both directions). This answers for CA; for MO/OH/MA the derivation d-left-shoulder-any-lane-count still stands. ⸻ MassDOT (MA only, Quire 2026-09-23): YES — left shoulder 4 ft (8 desirable) on four-lane freeways, 10 ft on six-or-more-lane freeways (2006 Ch 5 §5.3.4.1). MA and CA agree on the 6+ step; the derivation still governs MO/OH.

questions.ask: How small can a channelising leftover be before it is paint (a flush marked area) rather than a raised island?
tried: fhwa-sa-13-027 → f-sa13027-island-raised-or-flush (no threshold; its numeric island rules are AASHTO-attributed, excluded)
questions.notes: No permitted source states a paint-vs-raised size. v1 decision (Grader's plan): no painted-island class; every JR raised — rationale cites f-sa13027-island-raised-or-flush + f-mutcd-island-means. ⸻ Caltrans (CA): a FLOOR for any channelizing island (50 sq ft, preferably 75) but NO size at which raised becomes paint — its raised-vs-painted choice is keyed to posted speed (> 40 mph: curbs discouraged) and setting (rural: paint). The question as asked stays open. ⸻ MassDOT (MA): floors of 50 sq ft urban / 100 sq ft rural with a side ≥ 15 ft, linear islands ≥ 2 ft wide — but again NO size at which raised becomes flush; raised is "ideal", flush "less preferably" and never a refuge. Open as asked, in both CA and MA.

questions.ask: May an island be raised (curbed) or painted?
questions.notes: Both are compliant; the kit's choice (v1: raised) is ours, not the standard's.

questions.notes: ANSWERED FOR CA ONLY (Caltrans, Quire 2026-09-23): the exit nose sits at the 23-ft separation point between diverging edges of traveled way (may move downstream, paved width ≤ 20 ft); the entrance inlet nose at the 14-ft point. questions.neededBy: H-3 Q8 (future ped path through islands)

findings.quote: For conventional State highways with posted speeds less than or equal to 40 miles per hour and AADTT (truck volume) less than 250 per lane that are in urban areas or rural towns (rural main streets), the minimum lane width shall be 11 feet. The preferred lane width is 12 feet.

findings.question: q-freeway-inside-shoulder-3plus

findings.question: q-ramp-section

value.condition: reductions only on concurrence that a restrictive situation exists

findings.quote: Shoulder Width. Shoulder widths for ramps shall be as indicated in Table 302.1. Typical ramp shoulder widths are 4 feet on the left and 8 feet on the right.
findings.scope: CA freeway ramps

findings.question: q-ramp-section

value.widenCondition: radius ≤ 350 ft with central angle > 60°; single lane, or rightmost lane of a multilane ramp

Where ramps have curve radii of 350 feet or less, measured along the outside edge of traveled way for single lane ramps or along the outside lane line for multilane ramps, with a central angle greater than 60 degrees, the single ramp lane, or the lane furthest to the right if the ramp is multilane, shall be widened in accordance with Table 504.3 in order to accommodate large truck wheel paths.
findings.scope: CA freeway ramps

findings.question: q-ramp-section
findings.quote: The width of shoulders on single-lane and two-lane (except as described below) freeway-to-freeway connectors shall be 5 feet on the left and 10 feet on the right. … The width of shoulders on three-lane connectors shall be 10 feet on both the left and right sides.
findings.scope: CA freeway-to-freeway connectors

findings.quote: Radii for loop ramps should normally range from 150 feet to 200 feet. … Curve radii of less than 120 feet should also be avoided.
findings.scope: CA loop ramps

findings.quote: Typically, on-street parking areas in urbanized areas is included in the shoulder. … (7) Where on-street parking is allowed, 10 feet shoulder width is preferred.
findings.scope: CA conventional (non-freeway) multilane highways; left shoulder may be omitted at posted ≤ 35 mph (note 4)

findings.quote: A 2-lane, 2-way roadbed consists of a 24-foot wide traveled way plus paved shoulders. … Shoulder widths based on design year traffic volumes shall conform to the standards given in Table 307.2.
findings.scope: CA 2-lane State highways, new construction

findings.quote: Where there is little or no likelihood of managed lanes or transit facilities planned for the future, the minimum median width should be 46 feet.
findings.scope: CA; median width measured between inside edges of traveled way, INCLUDING the inside shoulders

paveIf.4 lanes: median ≤ 22 ft (22–30 ft only with barrier)

findings.quote: 6 or More Lanes--Medians 30 feet wide or less should be paved. (b) 4 Lanes--Medians 22 feet or less in width should be paved.
findings.scope: CA freeways

value.gore: area between a through roadway and an exit (or converging entrance) ramp

findings.scope: CA

findings.question: q-physical-gore-position
findings.quote: The exit nose shown on Figure 504.2B may be located downstream of the 23-foot dimension; however, the maximum paved width between the mainline and ramp shoulder edges should be 20 feet. … The paved gore area is typically that area between the diverging or converging edge of traveled ways and the 23-foot point.
findings.scope: CA freeway exits (single-lane standard design)

findings.question: q-physical-gore-position
findings.quote: On entrance ramps the distance from the inlet nose (14-foot point) to the end of the acceleration lane taper should equal the sum of the distances shown on Figure 504.2A.
findings.scope: CA freeway entrances

findings.question: q-gore-treatment

value.beyondPavedGore: contrasting surface treatment, distinguishable from any pavement meant for vehicles

findings.scope: CA freeway entrances and exits

findings.quote: In general, curbs should not be used on the high side of ramps or in off-ramp gore areas except at collector-distributor roads.
findings.scope: CA ramps

findings.question: q-island-min-size
findings.quote: Channelizing islands should not be less than 50 square feet in area, preferably 75 square feet. Curbed, elongated divisional median islands should not be less than 4 feet wide and 20 feet long.
findings.scope: CA intersections; a floor for ANY channelizing island (the text states no size at which an island switches from raised to painted)

findings.question: q-island-curbed-or-painted
findings.quote: On facilities with posted speeds over 40 miles per hour, the use of any type of curb is discouraged. … In rural areas, painted channelization supplemented with raised pavement markers may be more appropriate than a raised curbed channelization. … In urban areas, posted speeds less than or equal to 40 miles per hour allow more frequent use of curbed islands.
findings.scope: CA intersections — the raised-vs-painted choice is keyed to SPEED and setting, not island size

findings.quote: The approach end of each island should be offset 3 feet to the left and 5 feet to the right of approaching traffic, using standard 1:15 parabolic flares, and clearly delineated so that it does not surprise the motorist or bicyclist. These offsets are in addition to the shoulder widths shown in Table 302.1.
findings.scope: CA traffic islands; flares may be omitted on curved alignment for small triangular islands with sides < 25 ft

findings.quote: When a right angle cannot be provided due to physical constraints, the interior angle should be designed as close to 90 degrees as is practical, but should not be less than 75 degrees.
findings.scope: CA intersections incl. ramp termini

findings.quote: If the isolated off-ramp is necessary, the leading curb return from the perspective of a vehicle on the crossroad approaching from the same side as the off-ramp is made with a short radius curve of 3 to 5 feet.
findings.scope: CA isolated off-ramp terminals

findings.quote: Cul-de-Sac Street--A local street open at one end only, with special provisions for turning around.
findings.scope: The HDM DEFINES a cul-de-sac (and "Dead End Street/No Outlet … without special provisions for turning around") but gives no turning-circle geometry; local streets defer to locally adopted standards (Index 308.1).

findings.question: q-roundabout-geometry
findings.quote: Roundabout intersections on the State highway system must be developed and evaluated in accordance with National Cooperative Highway Research Program (NCHRP) Report 672 entitled “Roundabouts: An Informational Guide, Second Edition” dated October 2010 and Traffic Operations Policy Directive (TOPD) Number 13-02.
findings.scope: CA — the design METHOD is NCHRP 672 (not permitted) and "performance-based", Index 405.10(21); the values below are Caltrans's own typical ranges

findings.question: q-roundabout-geometry
findings.quote: The ICD for a single lane roundabout generally ranges between 105 feet to 150 feet to accommodate the California Legal design vehicle and 130 feet to 180 feet to accommodate the STAA design vehicle.
findings.scope: CA roundabouts; "The ICD ranges given above are typical values; the design may be larger or smaller."

findings.quote: With an inscribed circle diameter of less than 90 feet, the central island will need to be fully traversable to accommodate the design vehicles movements.
findings.scope: CA mini-roundabouts (low-volume routes, ramp terminals)

findings.question: q-roundabout-geometry
findings.quote: The total length of the raised island should be at least 50 feet although 100 feet is desirable. … The splitter island width should be a minimum of 6 feet at the pedestrian crossing to adequately provide refuge for pedestrians.
findings.scope: CA roundabouts — splitter islands required on all legs (may be dropped at a low-volume driveway leg)

findings.quote: A landscape buffer/strip, detectable by cane and under foot, between the sidewalk and the back of curb for the circular roadway of the roundabout should be a minimum of 2 feet wide, 3 feet is preferred.
findings.scope: CA roundabouts

findings.quote: A domed or mounded central island, between 3.5 to 6 feet high, is needed to focus attention on the approach and through roundabout alignment.
findings.scope: CA roundabouts

findings.question: q-sidewalk-default
findings.quote: The minimum width of a sidewalk should be 8 feet between a curb and a building when in urban and rural main street place types. For all other locations the minimum width of sidewalk should be 6 feet when contiguous to a curb or 5 feet when separated by a planting strip. Sidewalk width does not include curbs.
findings.scope: CA State highway right of way

findings.question: q-treelawn-default
findings.quote: The design of sidewalks and walkways varies depending on the setting, standards, and requirements of local agencies.
findings.scope: CA — the HDM names a planting strip (sidewalk 5 ft behind one) but states no planting-strip width

findings.quote: Vertical curbs are nearly vertical (approximate batter of 1:4) and vary in height from 4 inches to 8 inches. Sloped curbs (approximate batter of 2:3 or flatter) vary in height from 3 inches to 6 inches.
findings.scope: CA State highways

findings.question: q-curb-width
findings.quote: The curb sections provided on the Standard Plans are approved types to be used as stated below.
findings.scope: CA — the HDM gives curb HEIGHTS and types but no top-of-curb width; the sections are in the Caltrans Standard Plans (not in this registry)

findings.quote: Gutter pans are typically 2 feet wide but may be 1 foot to 4 feet in width, with a cross slope of typically 8.33 percent to increase the hydraulic capacity.
findings.scope: CA

value.urbanMedianAtOrBelow35mph: no offset if no gutter pan

findings.quote: The offset from the edge of traveled way to the face of curb or dike flow line should be no less than the shoulder width, as set forth in Table 302.1.
findings.scope: CA

findings.question: q-refuge-width

value.warrant: unsignalized, crossing 2+ through lanes in one direction

findings.quote: Traffic islands used as pedestrian refuge are to be large enough to provide a minimum of 6 feet in the direction of pedestrian travel, without exception.
findings.scope: CA intersections

findings.quote: When curb ramps are constructed or reconstructed, one curb ramp should be provided for each pedestrian street crossing.
findings.scope: CA; ramp design itself defers to the Standard Plans and DIB 82 (Index 105.5(3))

findings.quote: The curb face of the bulbout should be setback a minimum of 2 feet as shown in Figures 303.4A and B.
findings.scope: CA; bulbouts only where there is marked on-street parking, posted ≤ 35 mph

findings.quote: The lane width for both single and double left-turn lanes on State highways shall be 12 feet.
findings.scope: CA; 11 ft under the Index 301.1 urban exception; 10 ft right-turn lane only in severely constrained urban cases < 40 mph

value.rule: smallest radius that accommodates the design vehicle

findings.scope: CA city-street intersections; larger returns are set by the design-vehicle template, and "Local agency standards may be appropriate in urban and suburban areas."

findings.quote: The minimum width of local roads and streets that are to be reconstructed as part of a freeway or expressway project should conform to locally adopted standards except as described below.
findings.scope: CA — local street cross-sections are not the HDM's; they defer to local agency standards (and, on the NHS, to AASHTO — excluded, rule 5)

findings.question: q-culdesac-island-treatment
findings.quote: Cul-de-Sac Street--A local street open at one end only, with special provisions for turning around.
findings.scope: CA — the HDM says nothing about a turning circle's central island (treatment, surface or size); local streets defer to locally adopted standards (Index 308.1)

findings.question: q-culdesac-island-treatment
findings.quote: Unpaved areas (small unpaved areas should be avoided).
findings.scope: CA intersection traffic islands — NOT stated for cul-de-sac islands; the nearest statement the HDM makes

findings.question: q-freeway-inside-shoulder-3plus

findings.quote: Ramp Width: The typical width is 22 ft for one-lane ramps and 30 ft for two-lane ramps. … Ramps should have a lateral clearance on the right outside of the edge of traveled way of at least 6 ft and preferably 8-to-10 feet, and a lateral clearance on the left of at least 4 ft beyond the edge of the traveled way.
findings.scope: MA freeway ramps; the text gives the total ramp width, and the lane/shoulder split is only in Figures 7-22/7-23 (images)

findings.where: Ch 7 (Active Update web chapter) — §7.7 Ramp Design — Cross Section
findings.quote: Exit Ramp Entrance Width: Where the through lane and exit ramp diverge, the typical width will be 25 ft. This width will be maintained until the gore nose is reached and transitioned to the standard 22 ft width at approximately a 12:1 rate.

findings.quote: The minimum total width of the raised median should be 6 feet which allows for a 4-foot raised area with a 1-foot offset between the outside edge of the raised area and the travel lane.

gore: paved triangular area between through lane and exit lane
unpaved graded area beyond the gore nose

findings.quote: Thegore area is normally considered to be both the paved triangular area between the through lane and the exit lane and the unpaved graded area that extends downstream beyond the gore nose.

findings.where: Ch 6 (Active Update web chapter) — §6.7 Geometric Design Elements — Channelization Islands
findings.quote: Triangular islands should be a minimum of 50 square feet in surface area in urban areas and 100 square feet in surface area in rural areas with one side at least 15 feet in length. … Linear islands should be at least 2 feet wide. findings.where: Ch 6 (Active Update web chapter) — §6.7 — Right-Turn Channelization Islands

findings.question: q-culdesac-island-treatment

findings.question: q-culdesac-island-treatment

findings.quote: Medians in these circumstances are usually at least 10 feet wide to improve the health of the landscaping and to facilitate its maintenance.

findings.question: q-roundabout-geometry
findings.where: Ch 6 (Active Update web chapter) — §6.7 — Roundabout Geometric Design Elements
findings.quote: Planning and design of roundabouts is detailed in MassDOT’s Guidelines for the Planning and Design of Roundabouts
findings.scope: MA — a separate MassDOT document (not yet in this registry); Ch 13 also defers roundabout landscaping to its §5.7

findings.question: q-sidewalk-default

findings.where: Ch 3 (Active Update web chapter) — §3.3 Roadway Users — pedestrian spatial needs

findings.scope: MA

findings.question: q-treelawn-default
findings.where: Ch 5 (2006 EDITION) — §5.3.1.1 Sidewalks and Buffers (text + margin note)
findings.quote: Common widths of landscape buffer are between 2 and 6 feet, although larger buffers are possible. … As such, it is preferable that such buffers be at least 5 feet wide.
findings.scope: MA (2006 edition)

findings.question: q-treelawn-default
findings.where: Ch 13 (Active Update web chapter) — §13.4 — Back-of-Curb Planting
findings.quote: In general, planting strips less than 3.5 feet wide are too narrow for typical street trees species. … As recommended by urban forestry practices, aim for a buffer of at least 6 feet, preferably more.
findings.scope: MA back-of-curb tree planting

findings.question: q-curb-width
findings.where: Ch 6 (Active Update web chapter) — §6.7 — Channelization Islands (refuge dimensions)
findings.quote: The detectable warning surfaces are typically set at the back of curbs, which are typically 6 inches wide on either side.
findings.scope: MA — stated in passing while sizing an island refuge; the only curb-width statement in these chapters

findings.where: Ch 5 (2006 EDITION) — §5.5.3 Curbs, Berms and Edging
findings.quote: Barrier curbs range in height from 6-to-8 inches with a batter of 15:1 or steeper. Six inch curbs are typically used along roadways.
findings.scope: MA; Exhibit 5-16 (curb heights table) is AASHTO-adapted and excluded

findings.question: q-refuge-width
findings.where: Ch 6 (Active Update web chapter) — §6.7 — Channelization Islands; Left-Turn Lane Delineator Islands
findings.quote: They must be at least 7 feet wide in the direction of pedestrian travel to provide space for 2-foot-wide detectable warning surfaces with a 2-foot minimum gap between them.
findings.scope: MA; the authority MassDOT gives is PROWAG ("to meet PROWAG requirements"), itself a permitted source

findings.quote: Curb extensions should extend no further than 6 feet from the curb (see Chapter 16 for details).
findings.scope: MA; only with active curb-side uses (parking, transit)

value.below10_ft: local roads and some minor collectors only

findings.quote: The normal range of design lane width is between 10 and 12 feet. … Travel lanes narrower than 10 feet are only appropriate for local roadways and some minor collectors with very low traffic volumes and speeds. Lanes narrower than 9 feet are generally not recommended.

findings.quote: Minimum 4-foot shoulders are recommended for all arterials and collectors because of the value they provide for bicycle and pedestrian (particularly in rural areas) accommodation, and motor vehicle safety.
findings.scope: MA arterials and collectors; "Shoulders do not include on-street parking"

findings.quote: Parallel on-street parking requires a minimum of 7 feet of paved cross-section in addition to the required travel lane width and should not be permitted where this width is not available.

findings.where: Ch 5 (2006 EDITION) — §5.3.4.2 Arterials and Major Collectors
findings.quote: In most cases, the designer should provide a combined shoulder plus curb lane dimension of at least 14 feet so that motor vehicles can pass bicycles without changing lanes or swerving.
findings.scope: MA arterials and major collectors

findings.where: Ch 3 (Active Update web chapter) — §3.8 Controlling Criteria
findings.quote: MassDOT’s Controlling Criteria are described in Engineering Directive E-20-001
findings.scope: MA — the minimum-requirement values (lane width, shoulder width, pedestrian facilities…) live in E-20-001, not in these chapters

findings.question: q-sidewalk-default
findings.quote: Except as provided in R302.2.1 and R302.2.2, the continuous clear width of pedestrian access routes shall be 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum, exclusive of the width of any curb.

findings.quote: Where the clear width of pedestrian access routes is less than 60 inches (1525 mm), passing spaces shall be provided at intervals of 200 feet (61 m) maximum.
findings.scope: federal — all states, once adopted as standards by DOJ/DOT (36 CFR 1190.1)

findings.quote: The cross slope of a pedestrian access route not contained within a crosswalk shall be 1:48 (2.1%) maximum.
findings.scope: federal — all states, once adopted as standards by DOJ/DOT (36 CFR 1190.1); grade: "shall not exceed 1:20 (5.0%)" in highway right-of-way unless the adjacent street is steeper

findings.question: q-refuge-width

findings.question: q-refuge-width

findings.quote: A pedestrian access route complying with R302 shall be provided within and for the full length of a crosswalk, including medians and pedestrian refuge islands.

findings.quote: At an intersection corner, one curb ramp or blended transition shall be provided for each crosswalk, or a single blended transition that spans all crosswalks at the intersection corner may be provided.

findings.quote: The clear width of curb ramp runs (excluding any flared sides) and blended transitions not on shared use paths shall be 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.

findings.quote: Where pedestrian crossing is prohibited, curb ramps or blended transitions shall not be provided, and the pedestrian circulation path shall be either (a) separated from the roadway with landscaping or other non-prepared surface or (b) separated from the roadway by a detectable vertical edge treatment with a bottom edge 15 inches maximum above the pedestrian circulation path.
findings.scope: federal — all states, once adopted as standards by DOJ/DOT (36 CFR 1190.1)

findings.question: q-roundabout-geometry
findings.quote: Where pedestrian crossing is not intended, the pedestrian circulation path shall be separated from the curb, crosswalk to crosswalk, with landscaping or other nonprepared surface 24 inches (610 mm) wide minimum.
findings.scope: federal — all states, once adopted as standards by DOJ/DOT (36 CFR 1190.1)

findings.quote: Crosswalks at multi-lane channelized turn lanes shall provide treatments consisting of one or more of the following: a traffic control signal with a pedestrian signal head; a pedestrian hybrid beacon; a pedestrian actuated rectangular rapid flashing beacon; or a raised crossing.
findings.scope: federal — all states, once adopted as standards by DOJ/DOT (36 CFR 1190.1)
